Having been snared by the fowler of the afflictions,
Having been caught in the net of birth,
And having gone into the mouth of the Lord of Death,
How is it that you still do not know?

i.sp: Having been snared by the fowler of the afflictions
i.ev: ཉོན་མོངས་རྒྱ་པས་བཤོར་ནས། bshor = driven/chased (bo-kunpal 7-4: བཤོར་བའམ་དེད་ནས; bo-shenga: བཤོར་ཏེ་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས); the net (རྒྱ) is the next line's image; bo-gyaltsab glosses རྒྱ་བ as རྔོན་པ་ 'hunter'. 'Snared' pre-empts the net image.
i.fx: Having been driven down by the hunter of the afflictions,

atts.t:
Having been driven down by the hunter of the afflictions,
Having been caught in the net of birth,
And having gone into the mouth of the Lord of Death,
How is it that you still do not know?

That your own group is being killed one by one,
Have you not seen this?
Yet whoever relies on sleep
Is like an outcaste and a buffalo.

i.sp:
Yet whoever relies on sleep
Is like an outcaste and a buffalo.
i.ev: གཉིད་ལ་བརྟེན་པ་གང་། གདོལ་པ་དང་ནི་མ་ཧེ་བཞིན། is addressed to the same 'you' (ཁྱོད). All three commentaries read the comparison as the buffalo that sleeps unafraid while the outcaste kills others (bo-gyaltsab 7-5: གདོལ་བས་... གསོད་པའི་མ་ཧེ; bo-shenga: གདོལ་པ་དང་ནི་བསད་པར་བྱ་བའི་མ་ཧེ). English can be read as comparing the sleeper to both an outcaste and a buffalo.
i.fx:
Yet you who rely on sleep
Are like a buffalo beside its outcaste butcher.

atts.t:
That your own group is being killed one by one,
Have you not seen this?
Yet you who rely on sleep
Are like a buffalo beside its outcaste butcher.

When touched by hot water,
It is intensely hot for one with tender flesh;
Having created the karma of hell,
Why do you remain at ease like this?

i.sp: It is intensely hot for one with tender flesh;
i.ev: The Tibetan 'ཆུ་ཚན་གྱིས་ནི་རེག་པ་ན། གཞོན་ཤ་ཅན་ལ་རབ་ཚ་བའི།' is addressed to the listener (Sanskrit 'sukumāra pratapyase', 'you of tender body are scorched'); bo-gyaltsab 7-12 says the body of tender flesh must experience intensely hot suffering. The English line 2 introduces an impersonal 'It' and a generic 'one', losing the addressee.
i.fx: When touched by hot water, you of tender flesh are intensely scorched;

atts.t:
When touched by hot water,
You of tender flesh are intensely scorched;
Having created the karma of hell,
Why do you remain at ease like this?

The suffering of my accomplishing awakening
Has a limit;
To remove the harm of a splinter destroying from within,
It is like the suffering of making a cut in the body.

i.sp:
To remove the harm of a splinter destroying from within,
It is like the suffering of making a cut in the body.
i.ev: The Tibetan 'ཟུག་རྔུ་ཁོང་བརླག་གནོད་བསལ་ཕྱིར། ལུས་རྨ་བཏོད་པའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བཞིན།' makes the purpose clause qualify the cutting (Sanskrit 'naṣṭaśalyavyathāpohe tad-utpādana-duḥkhavat'); bo-shenga 7-22: 'ཟུག་རྔུ་ཁོང་བརླག་གི་གནོད་པ་བསལ་བའི་ཕྱིར། ལུས་ལ་རྨ་བཏོད་ནས...'. The English has a dangling infinitive and an unclear 'It'.
i.fx: It is just like the suffering of cutting open the body in order to remove the harm of a splinter that is destroying it from within.

atts.t:
The suffering of my accomplishing awakening
Has a limit;
It is just like the suffering of cutting open the body
In order to remove the harm of a splinter destroying it from within.

Because this, through the power of bodhicitta,
Exhausts previous misdeeds
And gathers an ocean of merit,
It is explained to be superior to the Śrāvakas.

i.sp: Because this,
i.ev: Tibetan འདི་ནི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས། — 'this' is the bodhisattva (bo-kunpal 7-29 བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་འདི་ནི; bo-gyaltsab 7-29 སྙིང་རྗེ་ཅན་འདི་ནི). English 'this' has no antecedent.
i.fx: Because this [bodhisattva], through the power of bodhicitta,

atts.t:
Because this bodhisattva, through the power of bodhicitta,
Exhausts previous misdeeds
And gathers an ocean of merit,
He is explained to be superior to the Śrāvakas.

To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, the forces
Are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment.
Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering
And by contemplating its benefits.

i.sp: contemplating its benefits
i.ev: དེ་ཡི་ཕན་ཡོན་ — 'its' is not clear after 'suffering'; bo-shenga 7-31 glosses དགེ་བ་ལ་གོམས་པ་དེ་ཡི་ཕན་ཡོན (benefits of virtue/aspiration), bo-kunpal 7-31 མོས་པ་དེ་ཡི་ཕན་ཡོན (benefits of that aspiration). English 'its' could be read as suffering's benefits.
i.fx: contemplating the benefits of that aspiration

atts.t:
To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, the forces
Are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment.
Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering
And by contemplating the benefits of that aspiration.

I have not made offerings to the Blessed One,
Nor provided the happiness of great festivals;
I have not performed service for the teaching,
Nor fulfilled the wishes of the poor.

i.sp: great festivals
i.ev: དགའ་སྟོན་ཆེན་པོ་ is singular 'great feast/festival' (Skt mahotsava); bo-shenga 7-37 glosses it as the Sangha's great feast (དགེ་འདུན་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་དགའ་སྟོན་ཆེན་པོ). English pluralizes.
i.fx: the great festival

atts.t:
I have not made offerings to the Blessed One,
Nor provided the happiness of the great festival;
I have not performed service for the teaching,
Nor fulfilled the wishes of the poor.

Habituated to that in any other life,
misdeeds and suffering will increase.
Any other deed and the time of the result
will become inferior, and that too will not be accomplished.

i.sp:
Any other deed and the time of the result
will become inferior
i.ev: Tibetan 'གཞན་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དུས་ཀྱང་ནི། དམན་འགྱུར་དེ་ཡང་འགྲུབ་མི་འགྱུར།'; bo-gyaltsab 7-48 reads 'ཕྱིས་བརྩམས་པའི་བྱ་བ་གཞན་དང་ ... འབྲས་བུའི་དུས་ཀྱང་ནི་དམན་པར་འགྱུར་བ་དུས་རིང་བོར་འགོར་བ་དང་། ལས་གཞན་དེ་ཡང་འགྲུབ་པར་མི་འགྱུར' (a later-begun other action; the result's timing is degraded/delayed; that other action is not accomplished). 'Any' is not in the Tibetan, and the English does not make clear which item becomes inferior or what 'that' refers to.
i.fx: Another deed, and the time of the result, will become inferior, and that other deed too will not be accomplished.

atts.t:
Habituated to that in another life,
Misdeeds and suffering will increase.
Another deed, and the time of the result,
Will become inferior, and that other deed too will not be accomplished.

For one who is despondent and abandons effort,
Is there liberation from destitution?
By generating pride and effort,
One is hard to defeat even by the great.

i.sp: One is hard to defeat even by the great.
i.ev: 'ཆེན་པོ་ཡིས་ཀྱང་ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ།' - bo-kunpal 7-53 'ལྟུང་བ་ཆེ༷ན་པོ༷ ... ཐུབ༷་པ༷ར་དཀ༷འ་བ་སྟེ'; bo-shenga 7-53 'སྤང་བྱ་ཆེན་པོ་ཡིས་ཀྱང་རྒྱལ་སྲས་དེ་ཉིད་ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ'; bo-gyaltsab 7-54 'སྤང་བྱ་ཆེན་པོ་ཡིས་ཀྱང་ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ' - the 'great' are great downfalls / great objects of abandonment, not great persons.
i.fx: One is hard to overcome even by great downfalls.

i.sp: liberation from destitution
i.ev: 'ཕོངས་ལས་ཐར་བ་ཡོད་དམ་ཅི' - ཐར་བ here is escape from hardship (bo-kunpal 7-53 'འདི་ཕྱི་ཀུན་ཏུ་ཕོངས་པ་ལས་ནམ་ཡང་ཐར་པ'), not soteriological liberation; 'liberation' risks a doctrinal misreading.
i.fx: escape from destitution

atts.t:
For one who is despondent and abandons effort,
Is there liberation from destitution?
By generating pride and effort,
One is hard to overcome even by great downfalls.

Just as one desires the joyful result of play,
Whatever is the action to be done,
One should be attached to that action,
And, unsated by that action, find joy in it.

i.sp: Whatever is the action to be done,
i.ev: 'འདི་ཡིས་བྱ་བའི་ལས་གང་ཡིན།' - 'འདི་ཡིས' (by this one, i.e. the bodhisattva) is unrendered; bo-gyaltsab 7-62 'བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་འདི་ཡིས་གཞན་དོན་བྱ་བའི་ལས་གང་ཡིན་པའི་ལས་'; bo-shenga 7-62 'བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་འདི་ཡི་བྱ་བའི་ལས་'.
i.fx: Whatever action is to be done by this one,

i.sp: the joyful result of play
i.ev: 'རྩེད་མོའི་བདེ་འབྲས' = the result that is happiness/pleasure of play (Skt krīḍāphalasukha; bo-shenga 'རྩེད་མོའི་བདེ་བའི་འབྲས་བུ'); བདེ(་བ) is locked as 'happiness', and 'joyful' attaches to the result rather than naming what the result is.
i.fx: the happiness that is the result of play

atts.t:
Just as one desires the happiness that is the result of play,
Whatever action is to be done by this one,
One should be attached to that action,
And, unsated by that action, find joy in it.

Like honey smeared on a razor's edge,
If one is not satiated by sensual desires,
With its ripening of happiness and peace,
How could one ever be satiated by merit?

i.sp:
With its ripening of happiness and peace,
How could one ever be satiated by merit?
i.ev: 'རྣམ་སྨིན་བདེ་ལ་ཞི་བ་ཡི། བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱིས་ལྟ་ཅི་སྟེ་ངོམས།' - 'རྣམ་སྨིན་བདེ་ལ་ཞི་བ་ཡི' modifies merit (bo-gyaltsab 7-64: merit gives happiness as ripening and leads to the peace of cessation). In the English 'With its ripening...' is a dangling modifier with no antecedent, and 'Like honey...' is likewise detached from 'sensual desires', which it qualifies ('འདོད་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས' ... 'སྤུ་གྲིའི་སོར་ཆགས་སྦྲང་རྩི་ལྟའི').
i.fx: By merit, whose ripening is happiness and which is peaceful, how could one ever be satiated?

atts.t:
If one is not satiated by sensual desires,
Which are like honey smeared on a razor's edge,
By merit, whose ripening is happiness and which is peaceful,
How could one ever be satiated?

Thinking, "How, in these situations,
Will mindfulness become a habit?"
For this reason, one should seek encounters
Or appropriate actions.

i.sp: one should seek encounters
i.ev: ཕྲད་པ is left without an object in the root, but bo-kunpal 7-73 (བླ་མ་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་ཕྲད་པ), bo-shenga 7-73 (མཁན་པོ་དང་སློབ་དཔོན་... དང་ཕྲད་པ) and bo-gyaltsab 7-73 (ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་འཕྲད་པ) all read it as meeting teachers or spiritual friends; Sanskrit saṃsarga is 'association'. Bare 'encounters' could be read as chance meetings of any kind.
i.fx: one should seek out meeting (with teachers and spiritual friends)

atts.t:
Thinking, "How, in these situations,
Will mindfulness become a habit?"
For this reason, one should seek out association
Or appropriate actions.

i.sp: one should seek out association
i.ev: ཕྲད་པ is "to meet/encounter": bo-kunpal 7-73 བླ་མ་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་ཕྲད་པ, bo-shenga 7-73 མཁན་པོ་དང་སློབ་དཔོན་...རྣམས་དང་ཕྲད་པ, bo-gyaltsab 7-73 དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་འཕྲད་པ. "Association" loses the single act of meeting a teacher/spiritual friend.
i.fx: one should wish to meet [a teacher or spiritual friend]

atts.t:
If one shares the same fortune as a childish one,
One will certainly go to the lower realm;
If they lead one to unequal fortune,
What is the use of relying on a childish one?

i.sp: If they lead one to unequal fortune
i.ev: སྐལ་མི་མཉམ་པར་ཁྲིད་བྱེད་ན: bo-shenga 8-9 (འཕགས་པ་རྣམས་དང་སྐལ་བ་མི་མཉམ་པར་ཁྲིད་པར་བྱེད་ན), bo-gyaltsab 8-9 and bo-kunpal 8-9 say the fortune is unequal to that of the noble ones, i.e. they lead one away from the noble ones' destiny. The bare 'unequal fortune' leaves the comparandum open and, following the previous line, reads as unequal to the childish ones' fortune.
i.fx: If they lead one to a fortune unlike that of the noble ones

atts.t:
If one shares the same fortune as a childish one,
One will certainly go to the lower realm;
If they lead one to a fortune unlike that of the noble ones,
What is the use of relying on a childish one?

Even this very body of mine,
By whose stench even foxes
Will not come near,
Will become exactly like that.

i.sp: Will become exactly like that.
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་ལྟ་བུར་ནི་འགྱུར་བར་འོང་ ('will come to become such'); the relative clause གང་གི་དྲི་ཡིས་... (by whose stench even jackals will not approach) qualifies the state the body will reach (bo-kunpal 8-30: ལུས་གང་གི་དྲིང་བ་... ཝ་... དྲུང་དུ་ཉེར་འགྲོ་མི་འགྱུར་བ་). The English leaves 'like that' without a clear antecedent, and 'exactly' has no counterpart in the Tibetan.
i.fx: Will come to be such that, by its stench, even foxes will not come near.

atts.t:
Even this very body of mine
Will come to be such that,
By its stench, even foxes
Will not come near.

Having made no friends and no enemies,
This body dwells alone in solitude;
Having reckoned it as already dead,
Even when dying, no one feels grief.

i.sp: Having reckoned it as already dead,
i.ev: The agent of the reckoning is others, not the body: bo-shenga 8-35 "ཉེ་དུ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་སྔ་ནས་ཤི་བ་དང་འདྲ་བར་བརྩིས་ན། ཤི་ནའང་དེའི་ཚེ་མྱ་ངན་བྱེད་པ་འགའ་ཡང་མེད་དོ"; bo-kunpal 8-35 "ཉེ་དུ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་སྔ་ནས་ཤི་བ་དང་འདྲར་བརྩིས་ནས". The English participle with "it" leaves the reckoner unclear.
i.fx: Being reckoned by relatives and others as already dead,

atts.t:
Having made no friends and no enemies,
This body dwells alone in solitude;
Being reckoned as already dead,
Even when dying, no one feels grief.

i.sp: no friends and no enemies
i.ev: འཁོན་པ is enmity/grudge, not "enemy"; bo-gyaltsab 8-35 བཤེས་མེད་ཅིང་གནོད་པ་བྱས་དོགས་པའི་ཁོན་པའང་མེད་པ (no friends and no grudge from suspected harm); Sanskrit avirodha "absence of hostility".
i.fx: Having no friends and no enmity,

i.sp: Being reckoned as already dead,
i.ev: Agentless participle dangles in English (reads as if "no one" is reckoned dead). bo-kunpal 8-35 ཉེ་དུ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་སྔ་ནས་ཤི་བ་དང་འདྲར་བརྩིས་ and bo-shenga 8-35 ཉེ་དུ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་སྔ་ནས་ཤི་བ་དང་འདྲ་བར་བརྩིས་ show the body is regarded as already dead by relatives and others.
i.fx: Since (I) am reckoned as already dead [by relatives and others],

atts.t:
Having let go of all other thoughts,
With a mind focused only on myself,
In order to settle the mind in meditative equipoise
And to subdue it, I shall strive.

i.sp: With a mind focused only on myself,
i.ev: "བདག་ལ་སེམས་པ་གཅིག་པུ་ཡིས" is explained as thinking solely of taming one's own mind / one's own practice: bo-shenga 8-38 "བདག་གི་སེམས་དུལ་བའི་ཐབས་ལ་སེམས་པ་གཅིག་པུ་ཡིས"; bo-kunpal 8-38 "བདག་གིས་རང་གི་སེམས་ལ་བལྟས་ཏེ"; Skt svacittaikāgramānasaḥ. "focused only on myself" can be read as self-concern.
i.fx: With a mind intent solely on my own mind,

atts.t:
Having let go of all other thoughts,
With a mind intent solely on my own mind,
In order to settle the mind in meditative equipoise
And to subdue it, I shall strive.

That face of your affliction,
just as it has now become manifest,
seeing it unveiled by vultures,
why do you flee from it now?

i.sp: That face of your affliction,
i.ev: bo-shenga 8-44 "ཁྱོད་ཉོན་མོངས་པར་གྱུར་པའི་གདོང་དེ" and bo-gyaltsab 8-44 "ཁྱོད་ཉོན་མོངས་ཤིང་ཆགས་པའི་གདོང་དེ" show the face is the one that afflicted you / that you were afflicted by and attached to; Skt tvatparikleśam. "face of your affliction" does not make this relation clear.
i.fx: That face which afflicted you (the face you were afflicted by),

atts.t:
That face which became your affliction,
Just as it has now become manifest,
Seeing it unveiled by vultures,
Why do you flee from it now?

i.sp: Just as it has now become manifest,
i.ev: ད་ལྟ་མངོན་སུམ་གྱུར་པ་བཞིན་ is "as if directly present now", a comparison (bo-shenga 8-44 ད་ལྟ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་གྱུར་པ་བཞིན་གྱི་རས་; bo-kunpal 8-44 མངོན་སུམ་དུ་གྱུར་པ་བཞིན་དུ). The English states it as an accomplished fact, and "became your affliction" for ཉོན་མོངས་པའི་གདོང་ (bo-shenga: ཁྱོད་ཉོན་མོངས་པར་གྱུར་པའི་གདོང་, the face you are afflicted by desire for) is loose.
i.fx: As if it were now directly before you,

atts.t:
If you have no attachment to impurity,
To a cage of bones bound by sinews,
Plastered with the mud of flesh,
Why do you embrace another in your lap?

i.sp: To a cage of bones bound by sinews, / Plastered with the mud of flesh, / Why do you embrace another in your lap?
i.ev: The Tibetan "རུས་གཟེབ་རྒྱུས་པས་སྦྲེལ་བ་ལ། ཤ་ཡི་འདམ་གྱིས་ཞལ་ཞལ་བྱས། གཞན" qualifies "གཞན" (another); bo-shenga 8-51 glosses it as "གཞན་བུད་མེད་ཀྱི་ལུས་" (the other woman's body). The English "To a cage of bones" reads as a dangling indirect object, so the syntax of the object is unclear.
i.fx: why do you embrace in your lap another—a cage of bones bound by sinews, plastered with the mud of flesh?

atts.t:
If you have no attachment to impurity,
Why do you embrace in your lap another—
A cage of bones bound by sinews,
Plastered with the mud of flesh?

If, with long hair and nails,
Yellowish teeth, and imbued with the foul smell of mud,
The nature of the body
Is terrifying indeed when naked,

i.sp: Yellowish teeth
i.ev: Tibetan "སོ་སྐྱ་དྲིར་བཅས" = yellowish teeth together with filth/foulness (བཅས). bo-kunpal 8-67: "སོ་སྐྱ་བོ་ ... དྲི་མར་བཅས་པ" and bo-shenga 8-67: "སོ་སྐྱ་བོ་དྲི་མར་བཅས་པ" (teeth with filth); Sanskrit "dantaiḥ samalapāṇḍuraiḥ". The English drops the filth on the teeth.
i.fx: yellowish teeth with filth

atts.t:
If, with long hair and nails,
Yellowish teeth with filth, and imbued with the smell of mud,
The nature of the body
Is terrifying indeed when naked,

Like a weapon that harms oneself,
Why do you make efforts to polish it?
Through the efforts of those deluded regarding the self,
This earth is completely agitated by madmen.

i.sp: to polish it
i.ev: "བྱི་དོར་བྱེད" means to tidy, clean and tend. bo-kunpal 8-68 glosses it as "ཁྲུས་དང་བྱུག་པ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་བྱི་དོར་བྱེད" (washing, anointing and so on) of the body. "Polish" fits a weapon but not the body, which is what "it" refers to.
i.fx: to tend to it (wash, anoint and adorn it)

atts.t:
Like a weapon that harms oneself,
Why do you make efforts to tend to it?
Through the efforts of those deluded regarding the self,
This earth is completely agitated by madmen.

i.sp: completely agitated
i.ev: ས་འདི་ཀུན་ཏུ་འཁྲུགས: ཀུན་ཏུ is "everywhere/throughout" (Kunpal 8-68: ཀུན་ཏུ་ཁྱབ་ཅིང་འཁྲུགས་པ, "pervading and agitating"), not an intensifier of the degree of agitation.
i.fx: agitated everywhere by madmen

atts.t:
For lustful persons, these and so forth
Are the many disadvantages, and the benefit is small,
Just as beasts that pull a cart
Eat only a few mouthfuls of grass.

i.sp: the benefit is small
i.ev: མནོག་ཆུང་ (Sanskrit alpāsvāda, 'little taste/relish'); bo-kunpal 8-79 glosses it as བདེ་བའི་མནོག་ཆུང་བ, a small taste of pleasure. མནོག is the savour of enjoyment, not 'benefit' (phan).
i.fx: and the enjoyment (gratification) is slight

atts.t:
For lustful persons, these and so forth
Are the many disadvantages, and the enjoyment is slight,
Just as beasts that pull a cart
Eat only a few mouthfuls of grass.

For the sake of that small benefit,
Which is not rare even for beasts to accomplish,
This perfect leisure and endowment, so difficult to find,
Is destroyed by those tormented by karma.

i.sp: that small benefit
i.ev: མནོག་ཆུང་ (Sanskrit āsvādalava) is a slight taste/relish of enjoyment; bo-kunpal 8-80 glosses it as མནོག་ཆུང་ལ་ ... ལོངས་སྤྱོད (food, clothing and other enjoyments). 'Benefit' misses this and is inconsistent with a proper rendering of མནོག.
i.fx: that slight enjoyment

atts.t:
For the sake of that slight enjoyment,
Which is not rare even for beasts to accomplish,
This perfect leisure and endowment, so difficult to find,
Is destroyed by those tormented by karma.

Having thus become weary of desire,
One should generate joy for solitude,
Empty of disputes and afflictions,
Within peaceful forests.

i.sp:
One should generate joy for solitude,
Empty of disputes and afflictions,
Within peaceful forests.
i.ev: རྩོད་དང་ཉོན་མོངས་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་པ། ཞི་བའི་ནགས་ཀྱི་ནང་དག་ཏུ། - 'empty of disputes and afflictions' qualifies the forests (bo-shenga 8-84: རྩོད་པ་དང་ནང་གི་ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་པ། ... ཞི་བའི་ནགས), but in the English the modifier follows 'solitude' and reads as describing solitude.
i.fx:
One should generate joy for solitude
Within peaceful forests
Empty of disputes and afflictions.

atts.t:
Having thus become weary of desire,
One should generate joy for solitude
Within peaceful forests
Empty of disputes and afflictions.

The fortunate ones, cooled by moonlight and sandalwood,
On delightful mansions of broad stone slabs,
Fanned by the silent, peaceful forest breeze,
Pace while contemplating the benefit of others.

i.sp:
The fortunate ones, cooled by moonlight and sandalwood,
On delightful mansions of broad stone slabs,
i.ev: ཟླ་འོད་ཙནྡན་གྱིས་བསིལ་བའི། ཡངས་པའི་རྡོ་ལེབ་ཁང་བཟང་ཉམས་དགའ་བར། - བསིལ་བའི་ modifies the stone-slab fine abode(s), not the fortunate ones (Sanskrit locative śītaleṣu ... śilātaleṣu; bo-shenga 8-85: ཟླ་བའི་འོད་ཀྱི་ཙནྡན་གྱིས་བསིལ་བར་གྱུར་པའི་ ... རྡོ་ལེབ་ཀྱི་ཁང་བཟང་). Also ཁང་བཟང་ཉམས་དགའ་བར is locative 'in/at' fine dwellings, not walking 'on' mansions.
i.fx:
The fortunate ones, in delightful fine dwellings of broad stone slabs
cooled by moonlight and sandalwood,

atts.t:
The fortunate ones, in delightful fine dwellings of broad stone slabs
Cooled by moonlight and sandalwood,
Fanned by the silent, peaceful forest breeze,
Pace while contemplating the benefit of others.

Acting independently and without attachment,
Unconnected to anyone at all,
Whatever joy of contentment one enjoys,
That is difficult even for Indra to find.

i.sp: joy of contentment
i.ev: ཆོག་ཤེས་བདེ་སྤྱོད་ - བདེ་ is 'happiness' (bo-kunpal 8-87: ཆོག་ཤེས་པའི་བདེ་བ; bo-gyaltsab: ཆོག་ཤེས་པའི་བདེ་བ), rendered 'happiness' elsewhere in this passage; 'joy' suggests དགའ་བ.
i.fx: happiness of contentment

atts.t:
Acting independently and without attachment,
Unconnected to anyone at all,
Whatever happiness of contentment one enjoys,
That is difficult even for Indra to find.

i.sp: If not, I too am like sentient beings.
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་མིན་བདག་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་བཞིན། is explained in bo-kunpal 8-102 and bo-shenga 8-102 as: if others' suffering is not to be averted, then my own suffering too, like that of other sentient beings, is not to be averted. The English leaves the point of comparison (non-aversion of suffering) unstated and reads as an unclear statement about the speaker's identity.
i.fx: If not, then I too am like other sentient beings (my own suffering is not to be averted either).

i.sp: If not, my suffering too is like that of sentient beings.
i.ev: དེ་མིན་བདག་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་བཞིན: the elided verb is བཟློག "averted": if it is not to be averted, then I too, like (other) sentient beings, am not to be averted/protected. Sanskrit na ced ātmāpi sattvavat; bo-kunpal 8-102: བདག་གི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་གཞན་གྱི་བཞིན་དུ་བཟློག་བྱ་མིན་པར་མཚུངས; bo-shenga 8-102: བཟློག་པར་མི་བྱའོ. The English "is like that of sentient beings" omits the conclusion that my own suffering would then also not be averted.
i.fx: If it is not (to be averted), then my own suffering too, like that of other sentient beings, is not to be averted.

atts.t:
Therefore, just as I protect myself
From even the slightest unpleasantness,
Likewise, a protective mind toward others
And a mind of compassion should be cultivated in this way.

i.sp: the slightest unpleasantness
i.ev: Tibetan མི་སྙན་ (Skt. avarṇa) is glossed in bo-kunpal 8-109 as མི་སྙན་པའི་ཚིག་ཙམ and in bo-shenga 8-109 as མི་སྙན་པ་བརྗོད་པ, i.e. an unpleasant or disparaging word, not unpleasantness in general.
i.fx: even the slightest unpleasant word

atts.t:
Therefore, just as I protect myself
From even the slightest unpleasant word,
Likewise, a protective mind toward others
And a mind of compassion should be cultivated in this way.

Having known oneself to have faults and others too
To be an ocean of good qualities,
One should meditate on completely discarding self-grasping
And taking up others.

i.sp:
Having known oneself to have faults and others too
To be an ocean of good qualities
i.ev: བདག་ཉིད་སྐྱོན་བཅས་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་། ཡོན་ཏན་རྒྱ་མཚོར་ཤེས་བྱས་ནས། — "too" (ཡང་) goes with others as an ocean of good qualities (Sanskrit parān api guṇodadhīn; bo-kunpal 8-112 gives self = faults, others = qualities); the English can be read as "oneself and others too have faults".
i.fx: Having known that oneself has faults, and that others too are oceans of good qualities,

atts.t:
Having known that oneself has faults, and that others too
Are oceans of good qualities,
One should meditate on completely discarding self-grasping
And taking up others.

Just as toward this body of selflessness,
Through habituation, the intellect of self has arisen,
Likewise, toward other sentient beings as well,
Through habituation, why would the intellect of self not arise?

i.sp: this body of selflessness
i.ev: བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ། — བདག་མེད་ modifies ལུས་ ("this body that is selfless/without self"; Sanskrit svakāye 'smin nirātmake; bo-shenga 8-114 བདག་མེད་པའི་ལུས་). "Body of selflessness" implies the body belongs to selflessness.
i.fx: this body, which is selfless (lacks a self)

atts.t: Just as towards this body of selflessness, The intellect of self has arisen through habituation, Likewise towards other sentient beings as well, Why should the intellect of self not arise through habituation?

i.sp: whole segment (single run-on line)
i.ev: The Tibetan is a four-line verse (བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ། / གོམས་པས་བདག་གི་བློ་བྱུང་བ། / དེ་བཞིན་སེམས་ཅན་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་། / གོམས་པས་བདག་བློ་ཅིས་མི་སྐྱེ།), but the English is one line with capitals after commas, so the line breaks are lost.
i.fx:
Just as towards this selfless body,
The intellect of self has arisen through habituation,
Likewise towards other sentient beings as well,
Why should the intellect of self not arise through habituation?

i.sp: this body of selflessness
i.ev: བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ: བདག་མེད་ here qualifies the body (Sanskrit nirātmake; bo-kunpal 8-114: བདག་མེད་པའི་ཕ་མའི་ཁུ་ཁྲག་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པའི་ལུས་འདི, a body without a self), so "body of selflessness" misleadingly makes selflessness a property or substance of the body.
i.fx: this selfless body

atts.t:
Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara,
Out of great compassion,
In order to dispel wandering beings' fear in assemblies,
Bestowed a blessing upon even his own name.

i.ev: འཁོར་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་བསལ་བའི་ཕྱིར། — the suffix འང "even" (Sanskrit pariṣacchāradyabhayam api) marks even the minor fear of timidity in assemblies (bo-kunpal 8-117 "བག་ཚ་བ་ཙམ་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་"); the English places "even" only on the name.
i.fx: In order to dispel even wandering beings' fear in assemblies,

atts.t:
Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara,
Out of great compassion,
In order to dispel even wandering beings' fear in assemblies,
Bestowed a blessing upon even his own name.

i.sp: even wandering beings' fear in assemblies
i.ev: འཁོར་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་བསལ་བའི་ཕྱིར: the emphasis (ཡང/ང) falls on the fear, even the slight timidity in assemblies (Sanskrit pariṣaccharadyabhayam api; bo-shenga/bo-gyaltsab 8-117: འཁོར་གྱི་ནང་དུ་བག་ཚ་བའི་འཇིགས་པའང་). The English placement of 'even' before 'wandering beings' suggests the beings are what is emphasised.
i.fx: to dispel even the fear (timidity) of wandering beings in assemblies

atts.t:
Through attachment to this body of mine,
Fear arises toward small sources of fear;
Toward that body which gives rise to fear,
Who would not be hostile as toward an enemy?

i.sp: be hostile as toward an enemy
i.ev: སྡང་མི་བྱེད། — སྡང་བ is "to hate/loathe" (Sanskrit na dviṣet; bo-kunpal 8-120 སྡང་བར་མི་བྱེད།), not "be hostile".
i.fx: hate as an enemy

atts.t:
Through attachment to this body of mine,
Fear arises toward small sources of fear;
That body which gives rise to fear,
Who would not hate as an enemy?

Whoever, for the sake of profit and respect,
Kills even their father and mother,
And, having stolen the wealth of the Three Jewels,
Will thereby be burned in the Avīci hell;

i.sp: Will thereby be burned in the Avīci hell;
i.ev: དེས་ནི་མནར་མེད་བསྲེག་འགྱུར་ན། — the clause ends in the conditional ན ("if"; bo-kunpal 8-122 ends "འགྱུར་ན"), continuing into 8-123's question. The English states it as an independent assertion.
i.fx: If one is thereby burned in the Avīci hell,

atts.t:
If one, for the sake of profit and respect,
Kills even their father and mother,
And, having stolen the wealth of the Three Jewels,
Is thereby burned in the Avīci hell,

"If I give, what will I consume?"
Thinking of one's own welfare is the way of a demon.
"If I consume, what will I give?"
Thinking of the welfare of others is the dharma of a god.

i.sp: the dharma of a god
i.ev: ལྷ་ཡི་ཆོས། — ཆོས here is "nature/way" parallel to འདྲེ་ཡི་ཚུལ (Sanskrit devarājatā "godliness"; bo-kunpal 8-124 ཆོས་ལུགས་བཟང་པོ, bo-shenga ལྷ་ཡི་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་པའི་ཆོས). "Dharma" suggests the Buddhist teaching.
i.fx: the way of a god

atts.t:
"If I give, what will I consume?"
Thinking of one's own welfare is the way of a demon.
"If I consume, what will I give?"
Thinking of the welfare of others is the way of a god.

I do all the work, and
this one remains in happiness itself.
This one is great in the world, and
I am known as inferior and without good qualities.

i.sp: all the work
i.ev: Tibetan ལས་རྣམས་བྱེད་པ་ is 'performing tasks/labors' (plural); no word for 'all'. bo-shenga 8-141 glosses these as menial labor (ཁུར་ཁྱེར་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དམན་པའི་ལས་རྣམས་).
i.fx: I perform the labors, and

atts.t:
I perform the labors, and
This one remains in happiness itself.
This one is great in the world, and
I am known as inferior and without good qualities.

i.sp:
This one is great in the world, and
I am known as inferior
i.ev: གྲག/གྲགས "is known/reputed" governs both clauses (Sanskrit kila after both mahān and nīcaḥ; bo-shenga 8-141: འཇིག་རྟེན་ལ་ཆེ་བར་གྲགས་པ; bo-kunpal: ཆེ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དང་ལྡན་པར་གྲགས་པ). The English asserts "great" outright and puts "known" only on the speaker.
i.fx:
This one is renowned as great in the world, and
I am known as inferior and without good qualities.

atts.t:
Dwelling in the jaws of vicious lower realms—
this one lacks compassion for such wandering beings.
Outwardly conceited about his good qualities,
he wishes to challenge wise persons.

i.sp: Outwardly conceited about his good qualities
i.ev: Tibetan ཕྱིར་ལ is 'furthermore/moreover' (Sanskrit aparaṃ), not 'outwardly'. bo-gyaltsab 8-145 frames it as 'ཕན་པ་མི་བྱེད་པར་མ་ཟད། ཕྱིར་ལ་རང་གི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཅན་དུ་རློམ་པ' (not only does he not help, but moreover he is conceited).
i.fx: Moreover, conceited about his good qualities

i.sp: Dwelling in the jaws of vicious lower realms— this one lacks compassion for such wandering beings.
i.ev: Tibetan ངན་འགྲོ་གདུག་པའི་ཁར་གནས་པ། འགྲོ་ལ་... : 'dwelling in the jaws...' qualifies the beings (འགྲོ), not 'this one'. bo-shenga 8-145: 'ངན་འགྲོ་གདུག་པའི་ཁར་གནས་པ། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྙིང་རྗེ་མེད་པ'; bo-kunpal 8-145 likewise. The English dangling participle reads as if this one dwells there.
i.fx: This one has no compassion for wandering beings dwelling in the jaws of the vicious lower realms.

atts.t:
Dwelling in the jaws of vicious lower realms,
this one lacks compassion for wandering beings.
Moreover, conceited about his good qualities,
he wishes to challenge wise persons.

Looking at one equal to me,
in order to make myself superior,
my gain and honor
will certainly be secured even through dispute.

i.sp: will certainly be secured
i.ev: Tibetan ངེས་པར་བསྒྲུབ is a resolve/obligation, not a prediction: bo-kunpal 8-146 'ངེས་པར་བསྒྲུབ་པར་བྱའོ', bo-gyaltsab 8-146 'ངེས་པར་བསྒྲུབ་པར་བྱའོ' (must be accomplished). Parallel verse 8-147 is rendered with 'I shall ensure'.
i.fx: I shall certainly secure, even through dispute,

atts.t:
Looking at one equal to me,
in order to make myself superior,
my gain and honor
I shall certainly secure, even through dispute.

If, in former times,
You had performed this action,
A situation like this, other than the perfect happiness
Of a Buddha, could not possibly occur.

i.sp: A situation like this, other than the perfect happiness of a Buddha, could not possibly occur.
i.ev: Tibetan 'སངས་རྒྱས་ཕུན་སུམ་བདེ་མིན་པ། གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲར་འགྱུར་མི་སྲིད།': 'མིན་པ' qualifies 'གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲ' (a situation like this that is not Buddha's perfect happiness). bo-gyaltsab 8-156: 'སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་དོན་གཉིས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་བདེ་བ་མིན་པ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མྱོང་བའི་གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲ'. The English 'other than' reads as an exception clause and obscures that the current suffering is what is not Buddha's happiness.
i.fx: such a situation as this, which is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha, could not possibly occur.

atts.t:
If, in former times,
you had performed this action,
what is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha—
such a situation as this could not possibly occur.

i.sp:
what is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha—
such a situation as this could not possibly occur
i.ev: སངས་རྒྱས་ཕུན་སུམ་བདེ་མིན་པ། གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲར་འགྱུར་མི་སྲིད: the situation (གནས་སྐབས) is one that is NOT the perfect happiness of a Buddha, i.e. suffering (bo-gyaltsab 8-156: སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་དོན་གཉིས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་བདེ་བ་མིན་པ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མྱོང་བའི་གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲར་འགྱུར་མི་སྲིད; bo-shenga 8-156). The English fragment "what is not..." followed by a dash does not make clear that it qualifies "such a situation".
i.fx: a situation such as this, which is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha, could not possibly occur.

atts.t:
Yet, even when instructed in that way,
If you, my mind, do not act like that,
Since all faults rely upon you,
You yourself will simply be subdued.

i.sp: You yourself will simply be subdued.
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཁྱོད་ཉིད་ཚར་གཅད་བྱ་བར་ཟད།' is obligation/only-remaining-option ('བྱ་བ' gerundive), not a bare future passive; bo-shenga 8-167: 'ཁྱོད་ཉིད་ཚར་བཅད་པར་བྱ་བ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་དོ'; bo-kunpal: 'ཚར་བཅད་པར་བྱ་བར་ཟད་དོ' (to be subdued by the antidote). Skt 'tvām eva nigrahīṣyāmi' has the speaker as agent.
i.fx: there is nothing left but to subdue you yourself.

atts.t:
Yet, even when instructed in that way,
if you, my mind, do not act like that,
since all faults rely upon you,
there is nothing left but to subdue you yourself.

From desiring the impossible, affliction
And shattered hopes will also arise.
Whoever does not depend on anything,
Their excellence is inexhaustible.

i.sp: shattered hopes
i.ev: བསམ་པ་ཉམས་པ means deterioration of one's intention/attitude, not disappointed hopes. bo-gyaltsab 8-175: "དགེ་བའི་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་བསམ་པ་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར" (wholesome intention degenerates); bo-kunpal 8-175: "བསམ་པ་ཉམས་པ་སྟེ་དཀོན་མཆོག་གི་དཀོར་རྐུ་འཕྲོག...ངན་སེམས" (stealing from the Three Jewels, malice); bo-shenga likewise "བསམ་པ་ཉམས་པ". 'Shattered hopes' follows Sanskrit āśābhaṅga, not the Tibetan.
i.fx: and a deteriorated intention

i.sp: does not depend on anything
i.ev: ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་མེད་པ is glossed by bo-shenga 8-175 as "ལུས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་པ་མེད་པར་གནས་པ" and by bo-kunpal as having no longing/expectation toward the objects of desire ("རེ་འདོད་ཀྱིས་ལྟོས་པ་མེད"); 'depend' could be read as independence rather than absence of expectation (Skt nirāśa).
i.fx: has no expectation of anything

atts.t:
From desiring the impossible, afflictions
and a deteriorated intention will also arise.
Whoever does not depend on anything,
their excellence is inexhaustible.

i.sp: Whoever does not depend on anything
i.ev: Tibetan གང་ཞིག་ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་མེད་པ; Sanskrit 'nirāśaḥ yas tu sarvatra' (without hope/expectation). Kunpal 8-175 glosses ཀུན་ལ་རེ་འདོད་ཀྱིས་ལྟོས་པ་མེད་པ (no looking-to with hope or desire) for all desirable things; Shenga ལུས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཀུན་ལ་ལྟོས་པ་མེད་པར་གནས་པ. 'Depend on' suggests reliance/need, whereas the sense is having no expectation or craving.
i.fx: Whoever has no expectation of anything

i.sp: From desiring the impossible
i.ev: Tibetan ནུས་མེད་འདོད་པ is 'desiring [what one] lacks the capacity [to achieve]'. Gyaltsab 8-175: འདོད་པ་རྫོགས་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་བཞིན་དུ་འདོད་པ; Kunpal སྒྲུབ་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་བཞིན་དུ་འགྲུབ་པར་འདོད་པ. 'The impossible' is stronger than lack of ability.
i.fx: From desiring what one lacks the ability to achieve

atts.t:
Even yogis, due to differences in intellect,
Are invalidated by those successively higher,
Through examples accepted by both,
Because they are unanalyzed for the sake of the result.

i.sp: Because they are unanalyzed for the sake of the result.
i.ev: འབྲས་བུའི་དོན་དུ་མ་དཔྱད་ཕྱིར: bo-shenga 9-4 explains "འབྲས་བུའི་དོན་དུ་མ་དཔྱད་པར་དེའི་རྒྱུ་ལ་འཇུག་པའི་ཕྱིར" (one engages in the causes without analyzing, for the sake of the result); bo-kunpal "འབྲས་བུའི་དོན་དུ་མ་བརྟགས་མ་དཔྱད་པར". The English leaves the subject of 'unanalyzed' unclear and reads as if the result is unanalyzed.
i.fx: Because, for the sake of the result, they are not analyzed.

atts.t:
Even yogis, due to differences in intellect,
are invalidated by those successively higher,
through examples accepted by both,
because, for the sake of the result, they are not analyzed.

i.sp: are invalidated by those successively higher
i.ev: Shenga 9-4 glosses the verb directly: "གནོད་ཅེས་པ་ནི་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་ཞེས་པའི་ཐ་ཚིག" ('harm' means 'overpower'); Kunpal 9-4 likewise "གནོད་ཅིང་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན". "Invalidated" narrows གནོད to an epistemic sense and loses the 'overpowering' sense given by the commentaries.
i.fx: are undermined (overpowered) by those successively higher

i.sp: because, for the sake of the result, they are not analyzed
i.ev: The Tibetan "འབྲས་བུའི་དོན་དུ་མ་དཔྱད་ཕྱིར" has no expressed subject; Shenga 9-4 reads "འབྲས་བུའི་དོན་དུ་མ་དཔྱད་པར་དེའི་རྒྱུ་ལ་འཇུག་པའི་ཕྱིར" (one engages the cause without analyzing, for the sake of the result), and Kunpal 9-4 "འབྲས་བུའམ་དགོས་པའི་དོན་དུ་མ་བརྟགས་མ་དཔྱད". The English passive "they are not analyzed" makes the examples/yogis the unanalyzed items.
i.fx: because, for the sake of the result, [people] do not analyze [them]

atts.t:
Even the direct perception of forms and so forth
Is through convention, not through valid cognition.
Regarding impurity and so forth,
That is false, like the convention of purity and so forth.

i.sp:
Regarding impurity and so forth,
That is false, like the convention of purity and so forth.
i.ev: Tibetan: དེ་ནི་མི་གཙང་ལ་སོགས་ལ། གཙང་སོགས་གྲགས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་རྫུན། The phrase 'regarding impurity' (མི་གཙང་ལ་སོགས་ལ) belongs with the convention of purity (གཙང་སོགས་གྲགས་པ), as bo-kunpal 9-6 shows (the body of a woman is impure, yet is conventionally called pure). The English attaches it to 'That is false', so 'purity regarding impurity' is lost.
i.fx:
That is false, just as the convention of purity and so forth
regarding impure things and so forth is false.

atts.t:
Even the direct perception of forms and so forth
Is through convention, not through valid cognition.
That is false, just as the convention of purity and so forth
Regarding impurity and so forth is false.

Merit from a Victor like an illusion
Is just as it is for one who is truly existent.
"If sentient beings are like illusions,
How are they born after dying?"

i.sp:
Merit from a Victor like an illusion
Is just as it is for one who is truly existent.
i.ev: Tibetan ཇི་ལྟར ('how?') in line 2 is the opponent's question, and ཇི་བཞིན ('just as') is the reply. bo-gyaltsab 9-9 and bo-kunpal 9-9 read the pair as objection plus answer. The English drops 'how' and gives only a flat statement, with no marking that the first part is the objection and the second part the reply.
i.fx:
"How is there merit from a Victor like an illusion?"
[Reply:] Just as it is for one who is truly existent.

atts.t:
"How is there merit from a Victor like an illusion?"
Just as it is for one who is truly existent.
"If sentient beings are like illusions,
How are they born after dying?"

"If, because it is seen by one endowed with other conditions,
It is luminous to itself,"
Through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
The vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.

i.sp: because it is seen by one endowed with other conditions
i.ev: Tibetan རྐྱེན་གཞན་དག་དང་ལྡན་པ་ནི། མཐོང་ཕྱིར: the one endowed with other conditions is the one who sees, namely other persons' minds. bo-kunpal 9-24 says those so endowed see the minds of other persons (གང་ཟག་གཞན་གྱི་སེམས་དག་ཀྱང་མཐོང་བའི་ཕྱིར), so one's own mind, which is nearer, should be luminous. bo-shenga 9-24 says the same. The English makes the mind 'it' the thing seen by such a person, which reverses agent and object.
i.fx:
If, because one endowed with other conditions sees [others' minds],
it is luminous to itself,

atts.t:
"If, because one endowed with other conditions sees,
it is luminous to itself,"
through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
the vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.

i.sp:
"If, because one endowed with other conditions sees,
it is luminous to itself,"
through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
the vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.
i.ev: Lines 1-2 are the opponent's (Cittamātrin) claim, lines 3-4 the reply (Shenga 9-24: 'འདིས་ཀྱང་ཤེས་པའི་རང་རིག་པ་གྲུབ་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བསྟན་པ'; Kunpal ཟེར་ན། དེར་མ་ངེས་ཏེ). The English runs the quoted objection straight into the reply with no break, and 'it' has no antecedent (the cognition/mind, Kunpal རང་སེམས).
i.fx: "If one endowed with other conditions sees [others' minds], then [the mind] is luminous to itself." [Not so:] through applying accomplished eye ointment, one sees the vase, yet it does not become the eye ointment itself.

atts.t:
If an illusion is not other than the mind,
And yet it is not conceived of as not other,
If it is an entity, how is it not other?
If it is not other, it does not exist as an entity.

i.sp: And yet it is not conceived of as not other
i.ev: Tibetan གཞན་མིན་པར་ཡང་མི་རྟག་ = "nor is it posited as non-other (identical)"; bo-kunpal 9-26 glosses སེམས་དང་གཅིག་ཡིན་པར་ཡང་མི་བརྟགས (not posited as one with the mind). "And yet ... not other" adds an adversative and the double negative hides that the claim is neither different nor identical.
i.fx: And it is not conceived as non-other (identical) either,

atts.t:
If an illusion is not other than the mind,
And it is not conceived as non-other either,
If it is an entity, how is it not other?
If it is not other, it does not exist as an entity.

i.sp: If an illusion is not other than the mind, / And it is not conceived as non-other either,
i.ev: The first couplet is the Cittamātrin objection (Kunpal 9-26 "སེམས་ཙམ་རྣམ་རྫུན་པ་ན་རེ"; Shenga 9-26 "ཅེ་ན། དེ་ཡང་རིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ"), and the Madhyamaka reply begins at "དངོས་ན་ཇི་ལྟར". The English runs objection and reply together without marking who speaks, unlike 9-27/9-30 where objections are quoted.
i.fx: "If an illusion is not other than the mind, / And it is not conceived as non-other either"— / If it is an entity, how is it not other? / If it is not other, it does not exist as an entity.

atts.t:
Just as an illusion, although not true,
Is what is seen, so too is the perceiving mind.
"If saṃsāra is based on an entity,
Otherwise it would be like space."

i.sp: Is what is seen, so too is the perceiving mind.
i.ev: Tibetan བལྟ་བྱ་དེ་བཞིན་ལྟ་བྱེད་ཡིད། and bo-kunpal 9-27 (ལྟ་བྱེད་ཡིད་ཀྱང་སྒྱུ་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་བདེན་མེད་ཡིན་ཀྱང་ལྟ་བྱེད་དུ་འཐད): the mind is the perceiver though untrue; English "so too is the perceiving mind" could be read as the mind also being seen.
i.fx: Is something to be seen, so too the mind is the one who sees.

atts.t:
Just as an illusion, although not true,
Is something to be seen, so too the mind is the one who sees.
"If saṃsāra is based on an entity,
Otherwise it would be like space."

When the mind is free of an apprehended object,
At that time, all are Tathāgatas.
Even if that is so, what merit is there
In conceptually constructing Cittamātra?

i.sp: what merit is there
i.ev: ཡོན་ཏན་ཅི་ཞིག་ཡོད: bo-kunpal 9-29 and bo-gyaltsab 9-29 gloss ཡོན་ཏན་ as དགོས་པ (purpose/benefit); Sanskrit guṇa. "Merit" suggests puṇya (བསོད་ནམས).
i.fx: what benefit is there

atts.t:
When the mind is free of an apprehended object,
At that time, all are Tathāgatas.
Even if that is so, what benefit is there
In conceptually constructing Cittamātra?

Even if one knows things to be like an illusion,
How will the afflictions be averted?
Since, toward an illusory woman,
Even her creator generates attachment.

i.sp: entire verse (unquoted)
i.ev: bo-gyaltsab 9-30 and bo-shenga 9-30 (…ཞེ་ན།) show the whole verse is the opponent's objection; other objections in this chapter are quoted, but here it reads as the author's own assertion.
i.fx: Put the verse in quotation marks as the objector's speech.

atts.t:
"Even if one knows things to be like an illusion,
How will the afflictions be averted?
Since, toward an illusory woman,
Even her creator generates attachment."

Her creator, toward objects of knowledge,
Has not abandoned the latent tendencies of the afflictions.
Therefore, when he sees her,
His latent tendency for emptiness is weak.

i.sp: His latent tendency for emptiness is weak.
i.ev: སྟོང་ཉིད་བག་ཆགས is locked as "latent tendency of emptiness" (used in 9-32); bo-gyaltsab 9-31 glosses སྟོང་ཉིད་རྟོགས་པའི་བག་ཆགས. "for" departs from the locked phrase.
i.fx: His latent tendency of emptiness is weak.

atts.t:
Her creator, toward objects of knowledge,
Has not abandoned the latent tendencies of the afflictions.
Therefore, when he sees her,
His latent tendency of emptiness is weak.

Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-fulfilling tree
Completely fulfill hopes,
Likewise, through the power of ones to be tamed and aspiration prayers,
The form of the Victor appears.

i.sp: through the power of ones to be tamed and aspiration prayers
i.ev: Tibetan གདུལ་བྱ་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས is "to those to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers"; bo-kunpal 9-35: གདུལ་བྱ་རྣམས་ལ་སྔོན་གྱི་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས་རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུར་སྣང་ངོ; bo-shenga 9-35: གདུལ་བྱར་ ... སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས. The English makes the disciples a second source of power alongside the prayers and drops that the Victor's form appears to them.
i.fx: Likewise, to those to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers, the form of the Victor appears.

atts.t:
Just as the wish-fulfilling jewel and the wish-fulfilling tree
Completely fulfill hopes,
Likewise, through the power of the ones to be tamed and aspiration prayers,
The form of the Victor appears.

i.sp: through the power of the ones to be tamed and aspiration prayers
i.ev: Tibetan གདུལ་བྱ་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས. Kunpal 9-35 reads དེ་བཞིན་གདུལ་བྱར་... སྔོན་གྱི་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས་རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུར་སྣང་ངོ་ (to the disciples, through the power of earlier aspiration prayers, the Victor's body appears); Shenga: གདུལ་བྱར་སྔོན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་གནས་སྐབས་ན་བཏབ་པའི་སྨོན་ལམ་གྱི་དབང་གིས་... རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུར་སྣང་ངོ་. The disciples are those to whom the form appears; the power is that of the (earlier) aspiration prayers. The English makes the disciples a causal power alongside the prayers and omits that the form appears to them.
i.fx: Likewise, to those to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers [made earlier], the form of the Victor appears.

atts.t:
Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-fulfilling tree
Completely fulfill hopes,
Likewise, to the ones to be tamed, through the power of aspiration prayers,
The form of the Victor appears.

In accordance with the conduct of awakening,
The shrine of the Victor has been accomplished;
Even when the bodhisattva has passed
Into nirvāṇa, it accomplishes all aims.

i.ev: Tibetan རྒྱལ་བའི་མཆོད་སྡོང་བསྒྲུབས་པ་ཡང་ and Sanskrit jinastambho 'pi: the particle ཡང (also/even) is not rendered; bo-kunpal 9-37 and bo-gyaltsab 9-37 link it to the garuḍa simile ("likewise").
i.fx: Likewise, the shrine of the Victor, too, is accomplished in accordance with the conduct of awakening;

atts.t:
Likewise, in accordance with the conduct of awakening,
The shrine of the Victor, too, has been accomplished;
Even when the bodhisattva has passed
Into nirvāṇa, it accomplishes all aims.

By whatever conditions you believe in that,
That is the same for the Mahāyāna as well.
If it is true because two others accept it,
The Vedas and so forth would also be true.

i.sp: because two others accept it
i.ev: Tibetan གཞན་གཉིས་འདོད་པས; bo-shenga 9-42: གཞན་གང་ཡང་རུང་བ་གཉིས (any two others), bo-kunpal 9-42 similarly གཞན་གང་ཟག་གང་ཡང་རུང་བ་གཉིས. "two others" does not make clear it means any two parties.
i.fx: because any two other parties accept it

atts.t:
By whatever conditions you believe in that,
That is the same for the Mahāyāna as well.
If it is true because any two other parties accept it,
The Vedas and so forth would also be true.

If being a monk is the root of the teaching,
Even being a monk is difficult to maintain.
For those whose minds have apprehension,
Even nirvāṇa is difficult to maintain.

i.sp: difficult to maintain
i.ev: Tibetan དཀའ་བར་གནས; bo-kunpal 9-44 glosses ཡོད་པར་དཀའ and ཐོབ་པར་དཀའ་བར་གནས (hard to exist / hard to attain); bo-gyaltsab 9-44: ཐོབ་པར་ཐལ (would not be attained). "Maintain" implies upkeep of an existing state, whereas the point is that such a monk/nirvāṇa is hard to realize or establish.
i.fx: is difficult to establish (hard to come by)

atts.t:
If being a monk is the root of the teaching,
Even being a monk is difficult to establish.
For those whose minds have apprehension,
Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.

If you say it is certain that, for the time being,
The craving for grasping does not exist,
Even if that craving is not afflicted,
Why would it not exist, just like delusion?

i.sp: The craving for grasping
i.ev: ཉེར་ལེན་སྲེད་པ: bo-kunpal 9-46 glosses ཉེར་ལེན་ as ཉེ་བར་ལེན་པའི་རྒྱུ་སྲེད་པ, i.e. craving that is the cause of grasping (Skt tṛṣṇā ... upādānam); grasping is not the object of the craving.
i.fx: the craving that is the cause of grasping

atts.t:
If you say it is certain that, for the time being,
The craving that is the cause of grasping does not exist,
Even if that craving is not afflicted,
Why would it not exist, just like delusion?

If any speech that accords with the sūtras
Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha,
Is it not asserted that most of the Mahāyāna
Is equal to your sūtras?

i.sp: accords with the sūtras
i.ev: ངག་གང་མདོ་སྡེ་ལ་འཇུག: འཇུག means enters/is included in (Skt sūtre ’vatared); bo-kunpal 9-49 and bo-shenga 9-49 read it as speech that enters/appears in the sūtra collection, not merely accords with it.
i.fx: enters the sūtras

atts.t:
If any speech that enters the sūtras
Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha,
Is it not asserted that most of the Mahāyāna
Is equal to your sūtras?

i.sp: is equal to your sūtras
i.ev: "མཚུངས" (Skt tulya) means similar/comparable; Gyaltsab 9-49 says "རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་མི་མཉམ་ཡང་ ... མཚུངས་པར" (though not equal in every respect, it is similar). "Equal" overstates the claim.
i.fx: is similar to your sūtras

atts.t:
For the sake of those suffering through delusion,
Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear
To successfully remain in saṃsāra—
This is the result of emptiness.

i.sp: To successfully remain in saṃsāra
i.ev: འཁོར་བར་གནས་པ་གྲུབ་འགྱུར་བ: remaining in saṃsāra is what comes to be accomplished (Skt saṃsāre sidhyati sthitiḥ); the infinitive reads as a purpose of being freed, which the Tibetan does not state (bo-kunpal 9-52: ... འཁོར་བར་གནས་པར་འགྲུབ་པར་འགྱུར་བ).
i.fx: Remaining in saṃsāra is accomplished

atts.t:
For the sake of those suffering through delusion,
Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear,
Remaining in saṃsāra is accomplished—
This is the result of emptiness.

Thus, toward the position of emptiness,
Refutation is not appropriate.
Therefore, without any doubt,
One should meditate on emptiness.

i.sp: not appropriate
i.ev: འཐད་མ་ཡིན: འཐད་པ means tenable/valid (Skt nopapadyate); bo-gyaltsab 9-53 says refutation is untenable because it is harmed by reasoning, not that it is improper.
i.fx: is not tenable

atts.t:
Thus, toward the position of emptiness,
Refutation is not tenable.
Therefore, without any doubt,
One should meditate on emptiness.

Thus, sattva, rajas, and
Tamas are neither a son nor a father,
And it is not seen to have a nature
That possesses the apprehension of sound.

i.sp: it is not seen to have a nature
i.ev: དེ་ནི་སྒྲ་འཛིན་དང་ལྡན་པའི་རང་བཞིན་དུ་ནི་མཐོང་མ་ཡིན: bo-shenga 9-64 identifies the subject as གཟུགས་འཛིན་པ་པོ་དེ, the apprehender of form; English "it" has no clear referent after the plural sattva, rajas, tamas.
i.fx: that apprehender of form is not seen to have a nature

atts.t:
Thus, sattva, rajas, and
Tamas are neither a son nor a father,
And that apprehender of form is not seen to have a nature
That possesses the apprehension of sound.

i.sp: that apprehender of form
i.ev: The verse line "དེ་ནི་སྒྲ་འཛིན་དང་ལྡན་པའི། རང་བཞིན་དུ་ནི་མཐོང་མ་ཡིན" has only "དེ" (that); "གཟུགས་འཛིན" appears only in Kunpal/Shenga/Gyaltsab 9-64 as a gloss on the referent (Sanskrit "tasya"). It is inserted into the verse text without brackets.
i.fx: and that [apprehender of form] is not seen to have a nature that possesses the apprehension of sound

atts.t:
If, because an opposing condition has arisen,
Suffering does not arise,
Is it not established that the conception of feeling
Is merely conceptual clinging?

i.sp:
the conception of feeling
Is merely conceptual clinging
i.ev: ཚོར་བར་རྟོག་པ་མངོན་ཞེན་ཉིད། ཡིན་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་གྲུབ་མིན་ནམ། Sanskrit 'kalpanābhiniveśo hi vedanā' says feeling itself is conceptual clinging; bo-kunpal 9-91: ཚོར་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་ནང་གི་རྟོག་པ་ཡིས་... མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་... ཉིད་ཡིན་ — what is called 'feeling' is nothing but clinging due to conception. The English makes the 'conception of feeling' the thing identified with clinging.
i.fx:
that what is called feeling
is nothing but conceptual clinging

atts.t:
If, because an opposing condition has arisen,
Suffering does not arise,
Is it not established that what is called feeling
Is nothing but conceptual clinging?

Seeing or even touching
Is of a nature like a dream and an illusion;
Because it arises simultaneously with the mind,
Feeling is not seen by it.

i.sp:
Because it arises simultaneously with the mind,
Feeling is not seen by it.
i.ev: སེམས་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ཕྱིར། ཚོར་བ་དེ་ཡིས་མཐོང་མ་ཡིན། The one arising together with the mind is the feeling, and 'that' (དེ་ཡིས, Skt tena) is the mind (bo-kunpal 9-99: ཚོར་བ་དེ་སེམས་དེ་ཡིས་མཐོང་བ་མ་ཡིན; bo-shenga 9-99). English 'it ... it' could be read as the seeing/touching in line 1.
i.fx:
Because feeling arises simultaneously with the mind,
it is not seen by that mind.

atts.t:
Seeing or even touching
Is of a nature like a dream and an illusion;
Because feeling arises simultaneously with the mind,
It is not seen by that mind.

There is no feeler at all,
Therefore feeling does not exist in reality.
Thus, for this collection of selflessness,
How could it be harmed by this?

i.sp: for this collection of selflessness
i.ev: བདག་མེད་ཚོགས་འདི་ལ། — 'this collection that lacks a self' (bo-shenga 9-101: བདག་མེད་པ་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བའི་ཚོགས་པ་འདི་ལ; bo-kunpal: བདག་མེད་པར་ཕུང་པོའི་ཚོགས་པ). Sanskrit 'nirātmake kalāpe'. 'Collection of selflessness' treats selflessness as what is collected.
i.fx: for this collection, which is selfless (without a self),

atts.t:
There is no feeler at all,
Therefore, feeling does not exist in reality.
Thus, how could this collection of selflessness
Be harmed by this?

i.sp: this collection of selflessness
i.ev: bdag med tshogs 'di la: 'bdag med' modifies 'tshogs' (Skt nirātmake kalāpe, 'in this self-less collection'); bo-kunpal 9-101 glosses it as the aggregate-collection lacking a self (bdag med par ... ཕུང་པོའི་ཚོགས་པ). The English makes selflessness the content of the collection.
i.fx: this collection that is without self

atts.t:
A sprout arises from a seed, and
Just as the seed is known by that very sprout,
By the consciousness arisen from the object of knowledge,
Why is its existence not known?

i.sp: A sprout arises from a seed, and / Just as the seed is known by that very sprout, / By the consciousness arisen from the object of knowledge, / Why is its existence not known?
i.ev: The verse is the opponent's objection: bo-kunpal 9-114 opens "ཡང་དེ་དག་འདི་སྙམ་དུ..." and ends "...ཅིས་མི་རྟོགས་ཏེ་རྟོགས་སོ་ཞེ་ན"; bo-shenga 9-114 ends "...ཅིས་མི་རྟོགས་ཞེ་ན། འདི་ནི་དཔེ་དང་འདྲ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ" (the reply comes in 9-115). The translation leaves it unmarked, whereas the parallel objections 9-106 and 9-109 are set in quotation marks, so the reader cannot tell who speaks.
i.fx: "A sprout arises from a seed, and / Just as the seed is known by that very sprout, / By the consciousness arisen from the object of knowledge, / Why is its existence not known?" (set in quotation marks as the opponent's objection)

atts.t:
"A sprout arises from a seed, and
Just as the seed is known by that very sprout,
By the consciousness arisen from the object of knowledge,
Why is its existence not known?"

Thus, regarding entities that are empty,
What is there to gain and what is there to lose?
By whom is respect shown,
Or what is there to be completely despised?

i.sp:
By whom is respect shown,
Or what is there to be completely despised?
i.ev: Tibetan གང་གིས་རིམ་གྲོ་བྱས་པའམ། ཡོངས་སུ་བརྙས་པའང་ཅི་ཞིག་ཡོད། has a single question 'what is there' governing both being honored by anyone and being despised (bo-shenga 9-151: སེམས་ཅན་གང་གིས་བསྟོད་ཅིང་རིམ་གྲོ་བྱས་པའམ། སྨད་དེ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྙས་པར་བྱས་པའང་ཅི་ཞིག་ཡོད). The English splits it into 'by whom is respect shown' and 'what is there to be despised', so the two parallel members no longer match and the agent 'by whom' attaches only to respect.
i.fx: What is there in being honored or utterly despised by anyone?

atts.t:
Thus, regarding entities that are empty,
What is there to gain and what is there to lose?
In being honored by anyone,
Or being utterly despised, what is there?

Furthermore, the incomparable, unbearable
Ocean of suffering is boundless.
There, one thus has little strength,
And there, the lifespan is also short.

i.sp: Furthermore,
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་ཡང་ (Sanskrit tatra ca; bo-kunpal 9-158 and bo-shenga 9-158 read དེར་ཡང་ 'even there') refers back to existence (srid pa) of the previous verse; 'Furthermore' drops the locative 'there'.
i.fx: There too,

atts.t:
There too, the incomparable, unbearable
Ocean of suffering is boundless.
There, one thus has little strength,
And there, the lifespan is also short.

Life passes quickly and meaninglessly,
And analysis is extremely hard to find.
Furthermore, as for habituation to distraction,
Where is the means to reverse it?

i.sp: Furthermore,
i.ev: Tibetan དེར་ཡང་ (Sanskrit tatrāpi; bo-kunpal 9-160 འཁོར་བའི་གནས་དེར་ཡང་) means 'even there, in that place'; the same words are rendered 'Even there' in 9-159 and 9-161, but here 'Furthermore' drops the locative and breaks the anaphora.
i.fx: Even there, as for habituation to distraction,

atts.t:
Life passes quickly and meaninglessly,
And analysis is extremely hard to find.
Even there, as for habituation to distraction,
Where is the means to reverse it?

Thus, for those tormented by the fire of suffering,
Well-arisen from the clouds of merit,
With a rain of my own accumulation of happiness,
When will I pacify them?

i.sp:
for those tormented by the fire of suffering,
Well-arisen from the clouds of merit,
i.ev: Tibetan བསོད་ནམས་སྤྲིན་ལས་ལེགས་འཁྲུངས་པའི། modifies རང་གི་བདེ་བའི་ཚོགས་ཆར ("rain of my own accumulation of happiness"), not the tormented beings; bo-kunpal 9-166: བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཚད་མེད་པའི་སྤྲིན་ལས་ལེགས་པར་བྱུང་བའི་རང་གི་བདེ་བའི་ཚོགས་ཆར; bo-shenga 9-166 likewise. In the English, the dangling line can be read as describing the beings.
i.fx: Well-arisen from the clouds of merit—a rain of my own accumulation of happiness—

atts.t:
Thus, for those tormented by the fire of suffering,
Well-arisen from the clouds of merit—
With a rain of my own accumulation of happiness—
When will I pacify them?

i.sp:
Thus, for those tormented by the fire of suffering,
Well-arisen from the clouds of merit—
With a rain of my own accumulation of happiness—
i.ev: In the Tibetan 'bsod nams sprin las legs 'khrungs pa'i' modifies 'rang gi bde ba'i tshogs char' (the rain), per bo-kunpal 9-166 and bo-shenga 9-166; in the English the participial phrase sits directly after 'those tormented...' and can be read as describing the beings.
i.fx: With a rain of my own stores of happiness, well arisen from the clouds of merit

atts.t:
By my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,
Through whatever virtue that is, may all wandering beings
Engage in the conduct of awakening.

i.sp:
By my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,
Through whatever virtue that is
i.ev: Tibetan has a single relation: བདག་གིས...བརྩམས་པ་ཡི། དགེ་བ་གང་དེས "by whatever virtue [arises] from my composing (the treatise) Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening"; bo-shenga 10-1: བསྟན་བཅོས་རྣམ་པར་བརྩམས་པ་ཡི། དགེ་བ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེས. The English gives two stacked instrumentals ("By my having composed... Through whatever virtue that is"), which reads as garbled.
i.fx:
Through whatever virtue there is in my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,

atts.t:
In my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,
Through whatever virtue there is, may all wandering beings
Engage in the conduct of awakening.

i.sp:
In my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,
Through whatever virtue there is
i.ev: The Tibetan 'bdag gis ... 'jug pa rnam par brtsams pa yi / dge ba gang des' = by whatever virtue [arises from] my having composed the Engaging; bo-gyaltsab 10-1 states the virtue is that obtained from composing the treatise. The English 'In my having composed ... through whatever virtue there is' does not make composition the source of the virtue.
i.fx:
Through whatever virtue there is in my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,

atts.t:
By the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water,
Seeing the burning embers of hell extinguished with a hiss,
And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction with bliss?"
May the hell beings behold Padmapāṇi.

i.sp: burning embers of hell
i.ev: Tibetan དམྱལ་བའི་མེ་མདག "the fire and embers of hell"; bo-shenga 10-12: དམྱལ་བའི་མེ་དང་མདག་མ་དག; bo-kunpal 10-12: དམྱལ་བའི་མེ་མདག. English drops "fire" as a separate item.
i.fx: fires and embers of hell

atts.t:
By the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water,
Seeing the fires and embers of hell extinguished with a hiss,
And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction with bliss?"
May the hell beings behold Padmapāṇi.

Likewise, by my roots of virtue, upon seeing Samantabhadra and other
Bodhisattvas' unobstructed clouds, and the bliss
And cool, fragrant rain they let fall,
May those sentient beings of hell become manifestly joyful.

i.sp:
and the bliss
And cool, fragrant rain they let fall
i.ev: Tibetan བདེ་བ་དང་། བསིལ་ཞིང་དྲི་ཞིམ་དང་ལྡན་ཆར་པ: "bliss" is one of the qualities of the rain (blissful, cool, fragrant), not a separate thing let fall; bo-shenga 10-15: རེག་ན་བདེ་བ་དང་། བསིལ་ཞིང་དྲི་ཞིམ་པོའི་ངད་པ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་ཆར་པ; bo-gyaltsab 10-15: བདེ་བ་དང་བསིལ་ཞིང་དྲི་ཞིམ་པ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་ཆར་བ. "the bliss and cool, fragrant rain" can be read as two nouns.
i.fx:
and the blissful,
cool, fragrant rain they let fall

atts.t:
Likewise, by my roots of virtue, upon seeing Samantabhadra and other
Bodhisattvas' unobstructed clouds, and the blissful,
Cool, fragrant rain they let fall,
May those sentient beings of hell become manifestly joyful.

i.sp: those afflicted by sorrow
i.ev: Tibetan མྱ་ངན་ཉམ་ཐག་ has two terms, sorrow and ཉམ་ཐག་ (distressed, wretched); bo-kunpal 10-20 glosses མྱ་ངན་གྱིས་གདུངས་ཤིང་ཉམ་ཐག་པ་རྣམས་, bo-shenga མྱ་ངན་གྱིས་ཉམ་ཐག་པ་; the English renders only 'sorrow'.
i.fx: those who are wretched with sorrow

atts.t:
In fearful, pathless wildernesses and the like,
Children, the elderly, the unprotected,
And those asleep, intoxicated, or insane—
May the gods protect them.

i.sp: intoxicated, or insane
i.ev: Tibetan མྱོས་ཤིང་རབ་མྱོས་རྣམས་ is 'intoxicated and utterly intoxicated'; bo-kunpal 10-26 རབ་ཏུ་མྱོས་པས་བག་མེད་པར་གྱུར་ཏེ (very drunk, hence heedless), bo-shenga མྱོས་ཤིང་རབ་ཏུ་མྱོས་པ; Sanskrit pramatta (heedless). Nothing says insane.
i.fx: intoxicated, or utterly intoxicated

atts.t:
In fearful, pathless wildernesses and the like,
Children, the elderly, the unprotected,
And those asleep, intoxicated, or utterly intoxicated—
May the gods protect them.

May they always meet with the Buddhas
And the children of the Buddhas.
With boundless clouds of offerings,
May they make offerings to the teachers of wandering beings.

i.sp: the teachers of wandering beings
i.ev: Tibetan 'འགྲོ་བའི་བླ་མ་མཆོད་པར་ཤོག' has no plural marker, Sanskrit 'jagadguru' is singular, and bo-gyaltsab 10-38 glosses it as the single 'འགྲོ་བའི་བླ་མ་སངས་རྒྱས'; the locked term 'teacher of wandering beings' is singular (the plural 'རྣམས' occurs only in the commentary's 'with retinue' gloss).
i.fx: the teacher of wandering beings

atts.t:
May they always meet with the Buddhas
And the children of the Buddhas.
With boundless clouds of offerings,
May they make offerings to the teacher of wandering beings.

May monasteries, with reading
And adorned with recitation, be well established.
May the Saṅgha always be in harmony,
And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.

i.sp:
May monasteries, with reading
And adorned with recitation, be well established.
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཀློག་པ་དང་། ཁ་ཐོན་གྱིས་བརྒྱན་' pairs reading and recitation as joint adornments of the monasteries (Sanskrit 'pāṭhasvādhyāyakalilāḥ'; bo-gyaltsab 10-42 'ཀློག་པ་དང་ཁ་ཏོན་གྱིས་དར་ཞིང་རྒྱས་'). The English splits them awkwardly ('with reading' / 'adorned with recitation'), which is hard to parse.
i.fx: May monasteries, adorned with reading and recitation, be well established.

atts.t:
May monasteries, adorned with reading
And recitation, be well established.
May the Saṅgha always be in harmony,
And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.

Disillusioned by broken ethical discipline,
May they always exhaust their misdeeds.
Having also attained a happy realm,
May their ascetic discipline not decline even there.

i.sp:
Disillusioned by broken ethical discipline,
May they always exhaust their misdeeds.
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བས་ཡིད་བྱུང་ནས' refers to those whose discipline has become corrupt who turn weary of it (bo-shenga 10-45 'སྔར་བསླབ་པ་ཉམས་པ་དག་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བས་ཡིད་བྱུང་སྟེ'; Sanskrit 'duḥśīlāḥ santu saṃvignāḥ'). The English has no stated subject, so 'they' wrongly picks up the ordained of the previous stanza, and 'disillusioned by broken ethical discipline' could mean disenchanted with the breaking of it.
i.fx: May those whose ethical discipline has been broken become weary of it, and always exhaust their misdeeds.

atts.t:
May those whose ethical discipline has been broken become weary of it,
And always exhaust their misdeeds.
Having also attained a happy realm,
May their ascetic discipline not decline even there.

As far as the limits of space in the ten directions,
In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings,
Just as Mañjuśrī acts,
May my conduct also be like that.

i.sp: As far as the limits of space in the ten directions,
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་ནམ་མཁའི་མཐས་གཏུགས་པའི། སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན' is an attributive phrase qualifying 'sentient beings' (Sanskrit 'daśadigvyomaparyanta-sarvasattvārtha'; bo-kunpal 10-54 'ནམ་མཁའི་མཐས་གཏུགས་པར་ཁྱབ་པའི་སེམས་ཅན་མ་ལུས་པ'). The English leaves the phrase as a dangling adverbial that can be read as modifying 'accomplish' or 'acts'.
i.fx: In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings, as far as the limits of space in the ten directions,

atts.t:
In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings
As far as the limits of space in the ten directions,
Just as Mañjuśrī acts,
May my conduct also be like that.

猶如漆黑夜晚密雲中，
剎那閃電展現極大光明；
同樣仰仗佛之威德力，
世間修福德之慧偶爾生起。

i.ev: Tibetan "བརྒྱ་ལམ་ན" means "among a hundred (occasions)"; bo-kunpal 1-5 glosses it as "བརྒྱ་ལམ་རེ་འགའ་ཞིག་ན ... བརྒྱ་ལན་རེ་སྟོང་ལན་གཉིས་ཙམ་འབྱུང་", i.e. once in a hundred times. The translation gives only "偶爾" (occasionally) for "ཐང་འགའ" and drops "hundred".
i.fx: 於百次之中偶爾生起

atts.t:
猶如漆黑夜晚密雲中，
剎那閃電展現極大光明；
同樣仰仗佛之威德力，
世間修福德之慧於百次之中偶爾生起。

欲摧毀百種有之苦，
欲遣除有情之不悅，
且欲享受百種眾多安樂者，
恆時皆不應捨棄菩提心。

i.sp: 不悅
i.ev: "མི་བདེ་བ" (bo-shenga 1-8: "སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་མི་བདེ་བ་མ་མཐའ་དག") is the opposite of "བདེ་བ", unhappiness/suffering, not "displeasure"; 不悅 reads as annoyance and does not contrast with 安樂 in line 3.
i.fx: 遣除有情之不樂

atts.t:
欲摧毀百種有之苦，
欲遣除有情之不樂，
且欲享受百種眾多安樂者，
恆時皆不應捨棄菩提心。

猶如殊勝形態之點金藥，
獲取此不淨之身，因其轉化為勝者之身
此一無價之寶，
故應極堅固地受持名為菩提心者。

i.sp:
獲取此不淨之身，因其轉化為勝者之身
此一無價之寶
i.ev: Tibetan: "མི་གཙང་ལུས་འདི་བླངས་ནས་རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུ། རིན་ཆེན་རིང་ཐང་མེད་པར་བསྒྱུར་བས་ན" - taking this impure body, (bodhicitta) transforms it into the Victor's body, a priceless jewel (bo-gyaltsab 1-10: "རྒྱལ་བའི་སྐུ་རིན་ཆེན་རིན་ཐང་མེད་པར་སེམས་དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བསྒྱུར་བས་ན"). The Chinese leaves the subject of 轉化 unstated and juxtaposes 勝者之身 and 此一無價之寶 without a link, with an unwarranted demonstrative 此一; hard to parse.
i.fx: 取此不淨之身，轉化為無價之寶——勝者之身，

atts.t:
猶如殊勝形態之點金藥，
取此不淨之身，轉化為
無價之寶——勝者之身，
故應極堅固地受持名為菩提心者。

眾生唯一商主以無量慧，
善加全面觀察見其極珍貴，
欲遠離眾生之處者，
應善加堅固受持珍貴之菩提心。

i.sp: 欲遠離眾生之處者
i.ev: "འགྲོ་བའི་གནས" here is the realm/state of migration: bo-shenga 1-11 "འགྲོ་བ་ལྔའི་གནས" (the five realms) and bo-gyaltsab 1-11 "འགྲོ་བའི་གནས་འཁོར་བའི་རྒུད་པ་མཐའ་དག" (all the miseries of saṃsāra). Sanskrit gatipattana. "眾生之處" can be read as "place of beings".
i.fx: 欲脫離諸趣之處者

atts.t:
眾生唯一商主以無量慧，
善加全面觀察見其極珍貴，
欲脫離眾生之處者，
應善加堅固受持珍貴之菩提心。

i.sp: 珍貴之菩提心
i.ev: Tibetan རིན་ཆེན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་ 'precious/jewel bodhicitta' (Skt. bodhicittaratnam); locked term རིན་ཆེན་ => 寶, but the translation uses 珍貴 and drops 寶. Gyaltsab 1-11 glosses it as 'རིན་པོ་ཆེ་དབང་གི་རྒྱལ་བོ་ལྟ་བུའི་རིན་ཆེན་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་' (a jewel-like bodhicitta).
i.fx: 寶菩提心

i.sp: 欲脫離眾生之處者
i.ev: Tibetan འགྲོ་བའི་གནས་དང་བྲལ་བར་འདོད་པ་ 'those wishing to be free of the migration-realms'; here འགྲོ་བ is 'destiny/realm of rebirth' (Skt. gati), not 'beings'. Gyaltsab 1-11 glosses འགྲོ་བའི་གནས་ as འཁོར་བའི་རྒུད་པ་མཐའ་དག་ (all the lower rungs/realms of saṃsāra); Shenga 1-11: འགྲོ་བ་ལྔའི་གནས (the realms of the five migrations). Applying the locked 眾生 gives 'places of beings', which is misleading.
i.fx: 欲脫離諸趣（輪迴之處）者

atts.t:
猶如欲前往與正前往，
能知兩者之間有差別，
如是智者對於此二者，
亦應次第了知其差別。

i.sp: 次第了知
i.ev: "རིམ་བཞིན" means "respectively, in due order of correspondence" (Skt. yathāsaṃkhyena; bo-kunpal 1-16 "གོ་རིམ་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན"; bo-shenga 1-16 "རིམ་པ་བཞིན"): each difference is understood for the corresponding member. 次第 suggests gradual/sequential learning.
i.fx: 依其各自對應而了知

atts.t:
猶如欲前往與正前往，
能知兩者之間有差別，
如是智者對於此二者，
亦應依其各自對應了知其差別。

由願菩提心，
輪迴之時雖生大果，
然不如行菩提心，
福德並不會相續生起。

i.sp: 然不如行菩提心，福德並不會相續生起
i.ev: Tibetan "ཇི་ལྟར་འཇུག་པའི་སེམས་བཞིན་དུ། བསོད་ནམས་རྒྱུན་ཆགས་འབྱུང་བ་མིན" = merit does not arise continuously as it does from engaging bodhicitta (bo-gyaltsab 1-17 "འཇུག་པའི་སེམས་ལས་བསོད་ནམས་བར་མ་ཆད་དུ་འབྱུང་བ་བཞིན་དུ ... མིན"). The Chinese 不如 reads as a comparison of quality and the clause is clumsy.
i.fx: 然福德並不像由行菩提心那樣相續不斷地生起

atts.t:
由願菩提心，
輪迴之時雖生大果，
然並不像由行菩提心那樣，
福德能相續不斷地生起。

從今而後縱睡眠，
抑或處於放逸中，
諸多福德之勢力，
無間等空廣生起。

i.sp: 無間等空廣生起
i.ev: Tibetan "རྒྱུན་མི་འཆད་པར་དུ་མ་ཞིག ། ནམ་མཁའ་མཉམ་པར་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་" = uninterrupted, manifold, arises equal to space. The Chinese string packs 無間 / 等空 / 廣 / 生起 together so that 等空 and 廣 are hard to attach (to 福德之勢力 or to the verb); 廣 has no Tibetan counterpart in the verse itself (only bo-kunpal 1-19 glosses རྒྱ་ཆེ་).
i.fx: 無間斷地、多重地生起，等同虛空

atts.t:
從今而後縱使睡眠，
抑或處於放逸中，福德之勢力，
無間斷、多重地，
生起等同虛空。

一一有情之不適，
欲將無量皆消除，
且於一一無量功德，
欲令成就何須言？

i.sp: 且於一一無量功德，欲令成就
i.ev: Tibetan "སེམས་ཅན་རེ་རེའི་མི་བདེ་བ། … རེ་རེའང་ཡོན་ཏན་དཔག་མེད་དུ། བསྒྲུབ་པར་འདོད་པ" : "each (sentient being) ... wishing to accomplish [each of them] as having immeasurable qualities". རེ་རེ refers to each sentient being, not to each quality. bo-kunpal 1-22: "དེ་དག་རེ་རེ་ལའང་ ... ཡོན་ཏན་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཉིད་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་པར་འདོད་པ"; bo-gyaltsab 1-22: "སེམས་ཅན་རེ་རེའང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་དཔག་མེད་ཅན་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་པར་འདོད་པ". The Chinese makes 一一 modify 功德 and leaves the beneficiary of 成就 unstated.
i.fx: 且欲令彼一一有情成就無量功德

atts.t:
一一有情之不適，
欲將無量皆消除，
且欲令彼一一有情，
成就無量功德何須言？

作為一切眾生喜樂之因，
化為治癒有情眾苦的良藥，
此種珍寶心的福德，
要如何能夠衡量？

i.sp: 喜樂
i.ev: Tibetan "དགའ་བའི་རྒྱུ" = cause of joy (དགའ་བ). 喜樂 contains 樂, the locked rendering of བདེ་བ, so it blurs དགའ་བ with བདེ་བ (bo-kunpal 1-26 and bo-shenga 1-26 list དགའ་བ and བདེ་བ as separate items).
i.fx: 歡喜

atts.t:
作為一切眾生歡喜之因，
化為治癒有情眾苦之良藥，
此種珍寶心的福德，
要如何能夠衡量？

向少數眾生施予尋常食，
僅於須臾間施予一餐食，
縱帶輕蔑且僅令飽半日，
世人亦敬奉其為行善者。

i.sp: 尋常食
i.ev: Tibetan "ནར་མའི་ཟས་སྦྱོར་བ" = providing food continuously/regularly. bo-kunpal 1-32: "ནར་མའི་ཞེས་ལོའམ་ཟླ་བར་ཉིན་བཞིན་ནར་མ་སྟེ་རྒྱུན་མ་བཅད་པའི་ཟས་སྦྱིན་པ" (nar ma = uninterrupted daily provision); bo-shenga 1-32 "དུས་ནར་མའི་ཟས". 尋常 means "ordinary", which is a different sense.
i.fx: 持續供應的飲食

i.sp: 縱帶輕蔑且僅令飽半日
i.ev: Tibetan "བརྙས་བཅས་ཉིན་ཕྱེད་འགྲངས་པར་བྱེད་པ" states as fact that the giving is with contempt (བརྙས་བཅས). 縱 turns it into a concession ("even if"), which the Tibetan does not have; bo-kunpal 1-32 "བརྙས་བཅོས་དང་བཅས་པའི་སྒོ་ནས" and bo-shenga 1-32 "སྦྱིན་པའི་ཚུལ་བརྙས་པ་དང་བཅས་པས".
i.fx: 帶著輕蔑而僅令飽半日

atts.t:
向少數眾生持續供應飲食，
僅於須臾間施予一餐食，
帶著輕蔑而僅令飽半日，
世人亦敬奉其為行善者。

若對如是勝者之子大施主，
有人生起惡心，則彼人
將依生起惡心之數量而於相應之劫，
住於地獄，牟尼如是宣說。

i.sp: 依生起惡心之數量而於相應之劫
i.ev: Tibetan "ངན་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པའི་གྲངས་བཞིན་བསྐལ་པར་ནི། དམྱལ་བར་གནས་པར་འགྱུར" = for as many eons as the number of malicious thoughts generated. 相應之劫 is vague and does not state that the number of eons equals the number of thoughts (bo-kunpal 1-34: "དེའི་གྲངས་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ་དེ་སྙེད་ཀྱི་བསྐལ་པར་ནི་དམྱལ་བར་... གནས་པར་འགྱུར").
i.fx: 生起惡心有多少次，便於地獄住多少劫

atts.t:
若對如是勝者之子大施主，
有人生起惡心，則彼人
生起惡心有多少次，便於多少劫，
住於地獄中，牟尼如是宣說。

天等世間中的香氣，
薰香、如意樹與寶樹，
未經耕作而生長的各類莊稼，
以及其他宜作供養的莊嚴物，

i.sp: 天等世間中的香氣
i.ev: Tibetan 'ལྷ་སོགས་འཇིག་རྟེན་ན་ཡང་དྲི་དང་ནི' contains the emphatic particle ཡང་ ('even in the worlds of gods etc.'); the Chinese gives a plain locative with no 'even/also'. Bo-shenga 2-4 likewise glosses 'ལྷ་དང་ཀླུ་ལ་སོགས་འཇིག་རྟེན་ན་ཡང་'. The meaning is intact, but the nuance is lost.
i.fx: 連天等世間中也有的香氣

atts.t:
連天等世間中也有的香氣，
薰香、如意樹與寶樹，
未經耕作而生長的各類莊稼，
以及其他宜作供養的莊嚴物，

猶如文殊師利等，
供養諸位勝者般，
我亦如是供養諸如來、
諸位怙主以及諸佛子。

i.sp: 供養諸位勝者般
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཇི་ལྟར་འཇམ་དབྱངས་ལ་སོགས་པས། རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ལ་མཆོད་མཛད་པ། དེ་བཞིན་' is a simple 'just as ... make offerings to the Victors, so (I)'. The Chinese doubles the comparison marker (猶如 ... 般) and leaves the clause dangling before 我亦如是.
i.fx: 猶如文殊師利等供養諸勝者，

atts.t:
猶如文殊師利等，
供養諸位勝者，
我亦如是供養諸如來，
諸位怙主以及諸佛子。

i.sp: 供養諸如來，諸位怙主以及諸佛子
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས། མགོན་པོ་སྲས་དང་བཅས་རྣམས་མཆོད 'the Tathāgatas, the Protectors, together with their children': མགོན་པོ is in apposition to the Tathāgatas. Gyaltsab 2-22: དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ལྷ་མི་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མགོན་པོ་སྲས་དང་བཅས་པ་རྣམས་ (Tathāgatas, protectors of gods and humans, together with their children). The Chinese '諸如來，諸位怙主以及諸佛子' reads as three separate groups.
i.fx: 供養諸如來怙主及其佛子

atts.t:
行於三世之諸佛，
偕同佛法與勝僧眾，
等同一切剎土微塵數，
我以俯首之身頂禮。

i.sp: 等同一切剎土微塵數，我以俯首之身頂禮
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཞིང་རྡུལ་ཀུན་གྱི་གྲངས་སྙེད་ཀྱི། ལུས་བཏུད་པ་ཡིས' = by bodies (plural) as numerous as all the atoms of the fields; bo-shenga 2-24 'ཞིང་ཁམས་རབ་འབྱམས་ཀྱི་རྡུལ་ཀུན་ཀྱི་གྲངས་སྙེད་ཀྱི། ལུས་རང་གི་བློ་ཡིས་སྤྲུལ་ནས' (emanated bodies equal in number to the atoms). The Chinese separates the number phrase from 身 and gives a single 'bowed body', so the quantity no longer clearly qualifies the bodies.
i.fx: 以等同一切剎土微塵數之諸身，俯首而頂禮

atts.t:
行於三世之諸佛，
偕同佛法與勝僧眾，
我以等同一切剎土微塵數之諸身，
俯首而頂禮。

於安住一切方所之
正等覺者與菩提心、
具大悲之諸尊前，
我合掌如此祈請：

i.sp: 正等覺者與菩提心、
i.ev: Tibetan 'རྫོགས་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས། ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་མངའ་རྣམས་ལ' uses བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས as an abbreviation of བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ (bodhisattvas): Sanskrit 'bodhisattvān'; bo-shenga 2-27 'ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་མངའ་བ'; bo-kunpal 2-27 'བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་ཐུགས་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་མངའ་བ'. The addressees are beings 'who possess great compassion'; the Chinese makes 'bodhicitta' (a mental state) one of the beings residing in all directions and addressed in prayer. The locked 菩提心 does not fit this occurrence.
i.fx: 於安住一切方所之正等覺者與菩薩，具大悲之諸尊前

atts.t:
於安住一切方所之
正等覺者與菩薩、
具大悲之諸尊前，
我合掌如此祈請：

我在罪業尚未淨除之時，
將在此之前死去；
如何能從此中獲得決定解脫，
祈請迅速救護我。

i.sp: 我在罪業尚未淨除之時，將在此之前死去
i.ev: Tibetan 'བདག་ནི་སྡིག་པ་མ་བྱང་བར། སྔོན་དུ་འགུམ་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་མཆི' = I will die before my misdeeds are purified (bo-gyaltsab 2-32: 'སྡིག་པ་མ་བྱང་བར་སྡིག་པ་དང་བཅས་ཏེ་འཆི་བདག་གིས་སྔོན་དུ་འགུམ་པར་འགྱུར'). The Chinese says 'at the time when misdeeds are not yet purified, I will die before this', which is circular/confusing about what 此 refers to.
i.fx: 我於罪業尚未淨除之前，便將先行死去

i.sp: 如何能從此中獲得決定解脫，祈請迅速救護我
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཇི་ལྟར་འདི་ལས་ངེས་ཐར་བར། མྱུར་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་བསྐྱབ་ཏུ་གསོལ' is a purposive petition: protect me quickly in whatever way I may be definitely freed from these (misdeeds). bo-kunpal 2-32 'ཐབས་ཇི་ལྟར་... ངེས་པར་ཐར་པར་འགྱུར་བ་ཞིག་མྱུར་ཞིང་རིངས་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་བསྐྱབ་པར་མཛད་དུ་གསོལ'. The Chinese 如何能... reads as a bare rhetorical question 'how can I be freed', detached from the request.
i.fx: 為使我能從此罪業中決定解脫，祈請以迅速之方式救護我

atts.t:
我於罪業尚未淨除之前，
便將先行死去；
為使我能從此罪業中決定解脫，
祈請以迅速之方式救護我。

必須捨棄一切而離去，
我由於未能如此了知，
為了親友與非親友之故，
造作了種種的罪業。

i.sp: 親友與非親友
i.ev: Tibetan 'མཛའ་དང་མི་མཛའི་དོན་གྱི་ཕྱིར' = for the sake of those dear and those not dear (enemies); bo-shenga 2-34 'མཛའ་བ་ལ་ཕན་འདོགས་པ་དང་མི་མཛའ་བ་ལ་གནོད་པར་བྱ་བ'; bo-kunpal 2-34 'མི་མཛའ་བ་དགྲ'. 非親友 would include neutral people, whereas the text means adversaries; the same pair is rendered 親友與怨敵 in 2-35 and 2-37.
i.fx: 為了親友與怨敵之故

atts.t:
必須捨棄一切而離去，
我由於未能如此了知，
為了親友與怨敵之故，
造作了種種的罪業。

面對尋常微小的懸崖，
尚且必須保持謹慎，
對於跌落一千由旬、
需長久停留的懸崖更何須多言！

i.sp: 需長久停留的懸崖
i.ev: The root has only ཡུན་རིང་གཡང་ས ('a long-lasting / long precipice'; Skt dīrghakālike prapāte, 'a precipice of long duration'). It has no modal 需 ('must') and no verb 'stay'. Shenga 2-57 glosses ཡུན་རིང་པོར་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མྱོང་བ ('experiencing suffering for a long time'); only Gyaltsab 2-57 spells out ཡུན་རིང་པོར་གནས་དགོས་པ ('must remain for a long time'). The Chinese puts one commentator's gloss into the root and reads as if one must linger on the cliff.
i.fx: 長久之懸崖

atts.t:
面對尋常微小的懸崖，
尚且必須保持謹慎，
對於跌落一千由旬之
長久懸崖更何須多言！

對於貧困匱乏的有情，
願我化為無盡藏，
成為種種所需資具，
安住於他們面前。

i.sp: 安住於他們面前
i.ev: Tibetan མདུན་དུ་ཉེ་བར་གནས་གྱུར་ཅིག: ཉེ་བར་གནས་ is 'remain close by / attend' (Sanskrit upatiṣṭheyam); bo-kunpal 3-9 and bo-shenga 3-9 gloss མདུན་ན་ཉེ་བར་གནས་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག as being near before them. The Chinese drops the nuance of nearness/attendance (the approved English has 'closely present').
i.fx: 親近安住於他們面前

atts.t:
對於貧困匱乏的有情，
願我化為無盡藏，
成為種種所需資具，
親近安住於他們面前。

不致損害彼等之行為，
無論什麼皆任其去做；
緣於我，無論何時，
願任何人都絕不致毫無意義。

i.sp: 願任何人都絕不致毫無意義
i.ev: Tibetan བདག་ལ་དམིགས་ནས་ནམ་དུ་ཡང་། འགའ་ཡང་དོན་མེད་མ་གྱུར་ཅིག: the point (bo-gyaltsab 3-14, bo-shenga 3-14 'རེ་བ་དོན་མེད་པར་མ་གྱུར') is that no one's connection with / reliance on me should be in vain. The Chinese makes 'anyone' the subject that becomes 'meaningless', which is hard to parse and does not show that it is the connection with me that must not be futile.
i.fx: 願無一人因緣於我而落得徒勞無益

atts.t:
不致損害彼等之行為，
無論什麼皆任其去做；
緣於我，無論何時，
願無一人落得徒勞無益。

願我成為無怙主者之怙主，
步入道者之嚮導，
欲渡水者之小舟、
船艦與橋樑。

i.sp: 小舟
i.ev: Tibetan has only "གྲུ" (boat) with no size marker. Both bo-kunpal 3-17 ("ཆུ་འབྲིང་པོ་ལ་གྲུ་བཟང་པོ", a good boat for medium water) and bo-shenga 3-17 ("ཆུ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་གྲུ་བ", a boat for great water) treat it as a sizeable vessel, so "小舟" (small boat) adds a size the Tibetan and commentaries do not support.
i.fx: 舟

atts.t:
願我成為無怙主者之怙主，
步入道者之嚮導，
欲渡水者之舟、
船艦與橋樑。

i.sp: 船艦
i.ev: Tibetan གཟིངས་ (in 'གྲུ་དང་ནི། གཟིངས་དང་ཟམ་པ') is a raft/float; bo-shenga 3-17 lists གྲུ་ for the large water, གཟིངས་ for the middling one, ཟམ་པ་ for the small. 艦 means a warship and has no support in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 舟、筏與橋樑

atts.t:
尋求洲島者，願我作洲島，
欲求床榻者，願我作床榻，
對於欲求奴僕之具身者，
願我成為彼等一切之奴僕。

i.sp: 床榻
i.ev: Tibetan "གནས་མལ" is a compound of dwelling + bed; bo-kunpal 3-18 glosses it "འདུག་པའི་གནས་དང་ཉལ་བའི་མལ" (a place to stay and a bed). "床榻" (bed/couch) covers only the "mal" half and follows the Sanskrit śayyā; English academic has the broader "resting place".
i.fx: 臥處

atts.t:
尋求洲島者，願我作洲島，
欲求臥處者，願我作臥處，
對於欲求奴僕之具身者，
願我成為彼等一切之奴僕。

我今日在一切救護者之
面前，已將眾生迎請為善逝果位
以及中途安樂之賓客，
願天與阿修羅等皆大歡喜！

i.sp: 迎請為善逝果位以及中途安樂之賓客
i.ev: Tibetan "བདེ་གཤེགས་ཉིད་དང་ནི། བར་དུ་བདེ་ལ་མགྲོན་དུ་བོས་ཟིན" means beings are invited as guests to (receive/enjoy) Sugatahood and interim happiness; bo-gyaltsab 3-33 glosses "ཚིམ་པར་ལོངས་སྤྱད་པས་ཆོག་པའི་འགྲོན་དུ་བོས" (invited as guests to be satisfied). The Chinese "為...之賓客" can be read as guests belonging to Sugatahood rather than guests invited to it.
i.fx: 已將眾生迎請為賓客，赴善逝果位以及中途安樂之筵

atts.t:
我今日在一切救護者之
面前，已將眾生迎請為賓客，
赴善逝果位以及中途安樂之筵，
願天與阿修羅等皆大歡喜！

任何他人哪怕只於一剎那，
對其福德製造障礙，
由於虧損有情之利，
其惡趣將無有邊際。

i.sp: 對其福德製造障礙
i.ev: Tibetan འདིའི བསོད་ནམས་ ('this one's merit') refers to the bodhisattva; bo-kunpal 4-9 and bo-gyaltsab 4-9 gloss it as བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔ་འདིའི་བསོད་ནམས་.
